RQ1.rationale: The paper gives a general CubeSat preliminary-design modeling approach and includes EPS sheets and power-component database categories, but it does not focus on EPS behavior or explicitly analyze minimal prior behavioral knowledge.

RQ2.rationale: It claims system-level outcomes for speed, cost, transparency, consistency, integration, and reuse, with some comparator metrics, but reliability/reproducibility/integrability are not evaluated as EPS-specific outcomes.

RQ3.rationale: The paper states that early integration enables verification to begin earlier and describes central consistency checks, but it does not provide EPS-specific verification procedures or pre-hardware test integration.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper itself links this approach to STAR/SPACE4YOU work and reports use on BOSS, Geo-Profundo, and a cislunar inspector mission; no prior extraction, bibliography, or external source was consulted.

implementation_pathway_tailoring.mapping_to_se_activities_lifecycle_gates: The adapted ESA CDF process maps to phase 0/A feasibility and preliminary design: requirements/drivers, ConOps trade, architecture definition, subsystem sizing, budgets, cost/risk, and baseline consolidation. implementation_pathway_tailoring.approach_classification_rationale: The approach integrates MBSE concepts with concurrent engineering, Excel-based parametric models, a central data exchange repository, COTS technology database, external analysis/CAD tools, and collaborative facility practices rather than relying on a single formal MBSE model.
tailoring_rationale: CubeSat missions need fast, cost-effective preliminary design.

COTS component databases support rapid technology-realistic subsystem selection.

practical_implementation_pathway.rationale: The paper provides a four-session implementation sequence, team roles/tools, and the BOSS case-study execution through baseline consolidation.

lightweight_resource_constrained_tailori.rationale: The approach tailors ESA CDF to four short sessions for CubeSat phase 0/A and uses spreadsheet/COTS database support, but resource constraints are not measured.

governance_project_deliverables_roi_valu.rationale: The paper links models to budgets, baseline decisions, risk/cost assessment, and cost/time comparisons, but lacks formal governance, ROI validation, or lifecycle gate evidence.

newspace_agile_distributed_rapid_iterati.rationale: Rapid, parallel, iterative design is central, with Jira/Miro noted, but the paper does not describe distributed agile ceremonies or NewSpace organizational deployment.

RQ1: General nanosatellite mission modeling is implemented as a phase 0/A concurrent workflow with standardized S3D spreadsheets, a central data repository, and CUTE-DB.
EPS is included as one S3D discipline and as multiple CUTE-DB power technology categories, but EPS behavior is not modeled in detail.
Limited early knowledge is handled by theory/formula sheets, typical values, user manuals, component property data, and shared assumptions rather than high-fidelity behavior models.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include faster feasibility analysis, lower estimated cost, lower mass, improved consistency, reduced manual effort/errors, better collaboration, and technology-realistic component selection.
Evidence is strongest for the BOSS one-case comparator metrics and weak for reliability, reproducibility, and integrability claims.
EPS-specific reliability or reproducibility outcomes are not reported; EPS relevance is via power components and budgets within system-level outcomes.
RQ3: Verification is discussed as an early benefit of model integration and as central-repository consistency checking.
The concrete mechanisms are common-input checks, sizing/budget validation, compatibility assessment, and figures-of-merit comparison before physical development.
No EPS-specific verification procedure, test case, hardware-in-the-loop, or requirements-to-verification traceability artifact is shown.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: The shown comparison uses only four concurrent sessions and not post-study refinement.
The S3D Tool needs improvement and optimization.
The Optical Payload calculation sheet needs updating and integration into the central repository.
Spreadsheets for other payloads need to be developed.
A dedicated C&DH calculation sheet must be created.
Comet and Matlab System Composer are being explored for enhanced MBSE and later-phase suitability.
MySQL and other database solutions are being evaluated to improve database management.
Mission Analysis and Structure & Configuration sheets are not linked to S3D spreadsheets and require manual input from external tools.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No formal SysML or equivalent MBSE language/model is reported.
No public availability of S3D, CUTE-DB, user manual, or case model data is stated.
No explicit EPS requirements model, power-behavior model, or EPS verification/test artifacts are provided.
The traditional-method comparator lacks methodological detail and independent validation.
No measured reliability, reproducibility, model-quality, or stakeholder-collaboration metrics are reported.
Toolchain continuity relies partly on manual transfers from STK/SolidWorks and informal presentations.

synthesis_consistency.notes_for_consistency_with_lineage: The paper's internal lineage is SPACE4YOU/STAR at Politecnico di Torino, with repeated use on BOSS, Geo-Profundo, and a cislunar inspection feasibility study. No external lineage or previous extraction was consulted under the silo rule.
synthesis_consistency.extraction_confidence_reason: The full Markdown paper was available and clearly describes the mission-level method, tools, workflow, and case metrics; confidence is lower only for EPS-specific verification because the paper largely does not report it.
